rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a baseline multimodal configuration with multiprofile support, standard encoders (scgpt and imagenet_vit_l), and simple aggregation/fusion methods. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modal baselines and provides a reference point for comparing more complex configurations. This is the best use of the first experiment as it balances exploration of the multimodal space with computational efficiency.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieved 51.76% accuracy. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation, a more complex method that could capture richer interactions between modalities. Transformer aggregation is a key design choice with potential for higher accuracy, and its cost (estimated higher than avgpool) is justified by the potential performance gain. This balances exploration of critical components while building on the multimodal/multiprofile foundation.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scgpt and imagenet_vit_l (config_001) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.5176). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 (more efficient) and using weighted fusion instead of concat, which may improve performance. It builds on the successful RNA encoder (scgpt) while exploring a cheaper image encoder and fusion method. Expected cost is moderate (similar to config_001 but lower than transformer-based models).

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.5176). This experiment tests changing the fusion method from concat to weighted, which could improve accuracy while maintaining similar cost. The weighted fusion might better capture interactions between modalities, and this configuration shares the same RNA/image encoders and aggregation as config_001, making it a low-cost, high-impact exploration of a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows config_049 (0.542 accuracy) is the best so far with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping scgpt RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders, which are proven effective. Transformer aggregation may capture more complex interactions, potentially improving accuracy. The expected cost is moderate (similar to config_001's 7.18 GPU hours), balancing exploration of a promising architecture with budget constraints.

Existing evidence shows config_049 (scgpt RNA, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.542). This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA encoder with the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion method to determine if RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance. It balances exploration (testing a new RNA encoder) with exploitation (using proven components) and is cheaper than transformer-based alternatives, preserving budget for future experiments.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_007) achieves high accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 (a larger, more parameter-heavy model) further improves performance. While resnet50 may increase training cost, it could yield higher accuracy. This balances exploitation of the scvi_n200's strength with exploration of image encoder variations, targeting the remaining budget efficiently.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests avgpool aggregation instead of transformer aggregation to determine if the aggregation method impacts performance. It clarifies the importance of aggregation type while keeping costs low (estimated ~5.5 GPU hours), balancing exploration of key design choices with budget constraints.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation (e.g., config_013 with 0.713 accuracy) are highly effective. This experiment tests scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion, which could clarify if combining these components improves accuracy further. It is the best use of the remaining budget as it explores a high-potential direction with moderate cost (estimated 5.5 GPU hours).

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (e.g., config_013, config_019) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests a similar setup with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, which could clarify if these components are optimal. It balances exploitation of proven components with minor exploration, and its estimated cost (~5 GPU hours) fits within the remaining budget.
